narrative.northStar: The Night Survey, seen through glass
narrative.overview: CarterLabs presents itself the way a surveyor sees a city at night: from altitude, in near-darkness, with only the structure that matters picked out. The ground is almost black. Mumbai's arteries are traced in a dim blood red, its hills in red contour lines from real elevation data, and Bandra's coast in bone-white surf that moves. Every mark on the map comes from OpenStreetMap or the terrain model. The map is the ground of the whole site: it never scrolls away. Over it floats one object: the island, a slab of liquid glass that carries all the content. It bends the map at its rim, frosts it in its body, and catches light on its edge from wherever the pointer is. It arrives as a Dynamic-Island pill (a live status: place and Mumbai time), springs open, and reshapes itself to fit each page as the visitor scrolls. The map is the world; the island is the instrument you read it through. Type carries the emotion. A tall condensed Didone (Onyx) speaks, a copperplate script (Edwardian) signs the word a sentence turns on, and a wide black grotesk (Archivo Expanded) says the name. Everything the hand touches, such as buttons, status and addresses, speaks the platform's quiet sentence-case sans (Geist). Measurements are set in a small tracked mono.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed, living map as the only background; scroll changes the island, never the world.
One liquid-glass island: refraction at the rim, frost in the body, pointer-lit specular edge, soft shadow.
Continuous corners and concentric insets; capsules for every control.
Blood red reserved for the story's turning points: the script word, the studio pin, the one action.
Motion as physics: springs for geometry, exponential ease-out for content.

rules.name: The Turning-Point Rule
rules.body: Blood red marks where the story turns: the script word, the live dot, the studio pin, the single primary action. If two red things compete on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Glass Is Light Rule
rules.body: Glass is never filled with a colour. Its presence comes from refraction, frost, rim light and shadow; any tint is darkness for legibility, never hue.

rules.name: The Signature Rule
rules.body: Script appears inside a line of Onyx, in Lit Blood, on the word the sentence turns on. Never set script alone, in bone, or at body size.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Brand faces (Onyx, Edwardian, Archivo) say things; Geist does things. Controls, status and addresses are always Geist, in sentence case.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Mono is only for numbers that measure something real. It is never used for flavour.

rules.name: The One Glass Rule
rules.body: There is one piece of liquid glass on screen, plus its page control. Content inside it does not become glass again. Platters are light on glass, not glass on glass.

rules.name: The Black Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black and fall downward. The only red light is the pin and the live dot.

dos: Do keep the map fixed; new sections are new island pages (`components/island/pages.tsx`), never new scrolling panels.
Do keep radii concentric: inner radius = island radius (40px) minus the inset.
Do use capsules for every control, and set their labels in Geist sentence case.
Do animate geometry with springs and content with exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`).
Do credit the map: © OpenStreetMap, OpenFreeMap, Mapzen terrain.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: the island appears open, and the surf and parallax are still.
donts: Don't nest glass in glass or put square cards inside the island.
Don't colour the glass; tint is darkness for legibility, never hue.
Don't use bezier overshoot or bounce easing; the springs already carry the life.
Don't set Edwardian or Onyx at body sizes, or script in bone.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't use cool greys or blue-blacks for neutrals.
